submission.justification: Sensor-T3 (planar, standard pitch) at 150 um gives the best single-hit resolution among the technologies that can meet the 97% hit-efficiency requirement at 2e16 neq/cm^2. Sensor-T1 is excluded because it reaches only 82.0% efficiency at end of life (strong charge trapping, full depletion not reachable at max bias), despite its better unirradiated resolution (6 um at 150 um). Sensor-T3 measured 98.5% at 2e16, a 1.5-point margin over the requirement. Sensor-T2 measured 99.2% (2.2-point margin) but its unirradiated resolution is about 13.9 um, roughly 55% worse than T3's 9.03 um at 150 um. Within T3, 150 um (9.03 um) and 200 um (8.98 um) are essentially equivalent on resolution. 150 um is chosen over 200 um because the earlier argument that thicker sensors retain more collected charge after irradiation was not supported, and 150 um needs a lower operating voltage and matches the 2025 baseline. Caveats: the 98.5% efficiency has no stated uncertainty and no stated sensor thickness, so efficiency at 150 um has not been directly verified and the margin is the tightest of the surviving options. The resolution figures are unirradiated simulation results only; end-of-life resolution is unknown. Before final sign-off, measure T3 efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm^2 at 150 um (ideally 200 um) and confirm it is at least 97%. If it is not confirmed, the fallback is Sensor-T2 at 100-125 um (about 13.9 um unirradiated). Sensor-T3 at 300 um should be avoided (about 12.1 um).

- **Why 200 µm rather than 150 µm:** This rests on a qualitative argument, not measured data. In the trapping-limited regime, absolute collected charge rises with thickness, so 200 µm should keep more signal after irradiation at a negligible resolution cost. This is not verified.

This changes the s4 choice of 200 µm. The s4 argument that collected charge rises with thickness after irradiation does not hold. In the trapping-limited regime, collected charge is roughly thickness-independent once thickness exceeds the trapping length, and a thicker sensor at fixed bias has a lower field and more trapping. 150 µm also needs less bias and matches the 2025 baseline, and the resolution cost is negligible.

- **Thickness:** 150 µm is inside the 50–300 µm range.
